residency.test: Resident if you have a domicile in Korea or a place of residence for 183 days or more in a tax year.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents, but a foreign resident who has had a domicile in Korea for five years or less in the last ten is taxed on foreign-source income only if it is paid in or remitted to Korea.
residency.flat_rate_election: Foreign employees may elect a flat 19% (20.9% including local income tax) on gross employment income with no deductions, for up to 20 years from first starting work in Korea.

headline.local_income_tax: an additional 10% of the income tax itself
headline.social_insurance: roughly 9.4% employee across pension, health, care and employment insurance
headline.foreign_flat_tax: 19% plus local tax, elective for foreign employees

standard_deduction.name: Employment income deduction
standard_deduction.note: approximation of the statutory five-tier formula, which is capped at 20,000,000

personal_allowance.name: Basic personal deduction
personal_allowance.note: 1,500,000 for the taxpayer and for each qualifying dependant

surcharges.name: Local income tax
surcharges.note: a flat 10% of the national income tax, collected with it

capital_gains.listed_shares: gains of small shareholders on listed shares traded on the exchange are exempt; large shareholders pay 20% to 25%
capital_gains.real_estate: 6% to 45% at ordinary rates with holding-period adjustments; heavy surcharges apply to multiple-home owners and to short holding periods
capital_gains.principal_residence: exempt up to 1.2bn won of sale price where the two-year holding and residence conditions are met
capital_gains.financial_investment_income_tax: the planned comprehensive financial investment income tax was repealed - confirm the current position before relying on older guidance

quirks: The flat 19% election for foreign employees ignores all deductions and credits. It wins at high salaries and loses at moderate ones - run both computations rather than assuming.
Year-end settlement (yeonmal jeongsan) in February is when employees reconcile the year. It is famously document-heavy, but the Hometax simplified service pulls most receipts automatically.
Credit card and debit card spending above 25% of salary generates an income deduction, which is why Koreans pay for almost everything by card.
Housing rent, monthly rent payments, and jeonse loan principal repayments all generate deductions or credits that foreign residents routinely fail to claim.
Severance pay is taxed under a separate, much lighter regime rather than as ordinary income.

reporting.who_must_file: Employees with a single employer are settled by the February year-end settlement and do not file. A May global income tax return is required for business income, multiple employers, or other income above thresholds.

deadlines.what: Year-end settlement (yeonmal jeongsan) with your employer for 2025
Extended deadline for taxpayers with an external audit requirement
Payment of the balance; instalments available above 10,000,000 won
Preliminary capital gains return on property

forms.name: Annual return filed in May via Hometax
Deduction declarations submitted to the employer in February
Employer certificate of income and tax withheld
Election for the 19% flat rate by foreign employees
Required where foreign accounts exceed 500,000,000 won on any month-end

documents_to_collect: Resident registration number or alien registration number, and Hometax certificate or simple authentication
The Hometax simplified year-end settlement data, which already holds card spending, insurance, medical and education payments
Housing lease contract and rent payment records
Details of foreign accounts and foreign income for residents past the five-year mark

penalties.late_filing: 20% of the tax due, or 40% where the failure is deliberate
penalties.understatement: 10% of the underreported tax, 40% for fraudulent reporting
penalties.foreign_account_report: up to 20% of the unreported balance

warnings: The employment income deduction is approximated; results below about 45,000,000 won of salary understate the deduction and therefore overstate tax.
Tax credits for children, pension savings, medical and education costs are not modelled and materially reduce the real liability.
The 19% flat rate election for foreign employees is not computed - compare it separately.
